title: Processing of identified student data
description: The Grades Portal Web App (P1) processes and transmits student id as part of the submission and grading request, which is identified information that directly identifies the data subject.
assumptions: Student id is a unique identifier for students in the system.

title: Transmission of unique identifier
description: The data flow from P1 to P2 includes student id, which is a unique reference to the identity of the data subject, transmitted across the system boundary.
assumptions: Student id serves as a unique identifier within the educational system context.

title: Linking through student identifier
description: The student id transmitted in the data flow can be used to link data across different systems and processes, potentially connecting submission data with other student records.
assumptions: Student id is consistent across systems and can be used for cross-system linking.

title: Quasi-identifier combination
description: The combination of student id, course, file reference, and requesting role in the data flow creates a quasi-identifier set that could potentially link to specific individuals through data correlation.
assumptions: The combination of these attributes may be unique or near-unique to specific students in certain contexts.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the size of the student population and course enrollment patterns.

title: Potentially sensitive data types transmitted
description: The data flow includes student id and file reference which may be more sensitive than strictly necessary for the grading service to perform its function.
assumptions: The grading service may not need full student identification or file references to process grading requests.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the specific functional requirements of the Assignment & Grading Service.

title: Data propagation to downstream service
description: Personal data (student id, course, file reference) is propagated from the Grades Portal Web App to the Assignment & Grading Service where it may be accessible by additional parties beyond the original collection context.
assumptions: The Assignment & Grading Service may have additional access to this data than the portal itself.

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: The data flow may process more personal data than functionally needed, as student id and file reference might be more granular than required for the grading service to perform its core function.
assumptions: The grading service could potentially operate with less identifying information.
uncertainty_note: Depends on the specific functional requirements and whether anonymized or pseudonymized data could suffice.

assumptions: Student ID is globally unique within the educational system

title: Data type sensitivity - student ID collection
